propositions: ADR-0083 prescribes isinstance-only capability detection against @runtime_checkable Protocols, which is safe on Python 3.11 but unsafe on Python 3.12+ because CPython switched to inspect.getattr_static, causing false negatives on dynamically-proxying objects.

The capability detection method returns isinstance True on Python 3.11 and False on Python 3.12 for the same proxy object and Protocol, creating a version boundary where previously correct guidance silently became unsafe.

A conforming caller using isinstance-only detection will skip writes when the proxy transport actually has the capability, resulting in silent soft failures that appear designed rather than erroneous.

The isinstance primary with member-level hasattr fallback pattern (isinstance(client, protocol) or hasattr(client, member)) is the sanctioned safe shape and is already implemented in _capability_present.

A tree-wide sweep found no other isinstance-against-Supports Protocol call sites; only dispatch_apply_phases.py:188 executes capability dispatch and it is already proxy-hardened with the hasattr fallback.
ADR-0083 requires amendment to document the version boundary, name the safe pattern, cite the reference implementation, and record that no other affected sites exist.
